observation_summary: The compiler crashes with an IllegalStateException during the ScopedAliases pass when processing JSDoc type annotations within a goog.scope block.
hypothesis: The compiler incorrectly processes JSDoc nodes multiple times because it duplicates JSDoc during declaration injection, leading to an inconsistent state in the alias processing logic.
prediction: The fix will introduce a mechanism to track injected declarations and ensure that JSDoc associated with these injected nodes is only processed once, preventing redundant or invalid alias applications.
experiment_rationale: The fix introduces a 'injectedDecls' set to track nodes and adds a conditional check in the JSDoc processing logic to skip nodes already present in this set. This confirms that the root cause was redundant processing of duplicated JSDoc nodes.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an incorrect algorithmic approach to processing JSDoc nodes. The compiler was blindly iterating over JSDoc nodes, failing to account for the fact that some nodes were duplicated during the injection process. This led to redundant processing and an inconsistent state, triggering the Preconditions check. The fix involves implementing a tracking mechanism (a Set) to ensure each node is processed exactly once, which is a correction to the procedural logic of the compiler pass.
evidence_used: The fix adds a 'injectedDecls' set to track nodes.
The fix adds a conditional check 'if (info != null && !injectedDecls.contains(n))' to prevent redundant processing.
The bug report mentions that JSDoc is duplicated multiple times and the compiler gets into a weird state where its internal bookkeeping is wrong.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the crash occurs at a Preconditions check, the check is merely a symptom of the underlying algorithmic flaw where the compiler's state becomes inconsistent due to redundant processing.
Although the fix involves maintaining consistency between injected nodes and JSDoc processing, the core issue is the procedural logic of how the compiler traverses and processes these nodes.
